key_insight: An isothermal-wall entropy fix adds total-energy density divided by wall temperature to the entropy, enabling entropy-stable no-slip wall formulations that preserve heat transfer and energy consistency in compressible Navier–Stokes flow.
engineering_relevance: This provides practical wall-boundary treatments for high-order CFD solvers that improve robustness and balance at hot walls, especially for turbulence and supersonic separated-flow simulations.
method: Affine entropy modification based on ballistic energy at constant wall temperature
Two DG-SBP-SAT wall formulations: complete-residual and Fourier-energy-exact
Entropy-consistent penalties and fluxes that enforce zero/nonpositive wall contributions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports pointwise identity tests, manufactured-solution convergence at order p_s+1, thermal-relaxation balance checks, and 3D simulations showing closed-domain balance and curved-wall convergence.
watch_item: The formulations assume a stationary, impermeable, no-slip wall at constant positive temperature, so implementation and applicability may be more limited for moving, permeable, or nonisothermal boundaries.
paper_title: Isothermal walls in the compressible Navier-Stokes equations: affine entropy, ballistic energy, and entropy-stable discrete formulations
